item.title: Truro's En-Neyah 'sitting up and chatting' after collapse
item.description: Morrocan-born En-Neyah is a former Republic of Ireland youth international [Shutterstock] Truro City midfielder Yassine En-Neyah is in a stable condition after collapsing during the warm-up for his side's National League South game on Saturday. The game between Folkestone Invicta and Truro was abandoned before kick-off due to the incident. The 26-year-old was taken by ambulance to the William Harvey Hospital in Ashford for treatment. "He is stable, sitting up and chatting, but will remain in hospital overnight under observation," a Truro City statement read. "The club would like to place on record its thanks to Truro City's medical staff, their counterparts at Folkestone Invicta, along with all club personnel from the home club. "Both the National League and Football Association have also offered their help and support. "There have also been many well wishes from Truro City fans and the wider football community too." En-Neyah joined Truro from Irish side Waterford in February 2023, having previously been on the books at Nottingham Forest. Truro were second in the table before this afternoon's matches, with Folkestone in 15th place. An update on En-Neyah's condition, and any rearranged date for the fixture, will be announced in due course. Related internet links Truro City FC

item.title: Norris takes pole in rain-delayed qualifying
item.description: Lando Norris has won two races this season, in Hungary and the Netherlands [Reuters] McLaren's Lando Norris took pole position for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix in a wet qualifying session at Interlagos delayed by nearly an hour and a half for heavy rain. Norris beat fellow Briton George Russell by 0.204 seconds, and the Mercedes driver was fuming that he could have been faster had he not been told by his engineer to abort a faster lap. In any case, Russell has a five-place grid penalty for exceeding his permitted number of engine parts, promoting team-mate and new world champion Kimi Antonelli to second. Ferrari's Charles Leclerc qualified fourth but has a 10-place grid penalty which promotes Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson to third. The New Zealander was one of a number of drivers to have their best qualifying session of the year thanks to the levelling effect of the wet weather. Also among them were Audi's Nico Hulkenberg, who qualified sixth and will start fourth, Haas driver Oliver Bearman, who was eighth and will start sixth, and Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso, who was ninth and will move up one place to eighth. item.title: F1 Brazilian GP: Lando Norris takes pole in soaking wet qualifying
item.description: Motorsport photo McLaren's Lando Norris has claimed pole in a wet qualifying session at Formula 1's Brazilian Grand Prix, beating George Russell on a treacherous Interlagos circuit. In a challenging session that was red-flagged by over an hour due to heavy rain and standing water, Norris topped the final Q3 shootout with a 1m27.470s lap on the intermediate tyres, pipping Mercedes' Russell by two tenths. Russell was nursing a five-place grid penalty for a power unit change, but was still incensed by his Mercedes team asking him to abort his second flying lap in Q3. Antonelli qualified third, six tenths behind Norris, with Charles Leclerc fourth in the Ferrari . As well as Russell's demotion, Leclerc's 10-place engine penalty elevated fifth-placed Racing Bulls driver Liam Lawson to third on Sunday's grid. Lawson is under pressure to retain his seat as Racing Bulls considers promoting reserve driver Nikola Tsolov instead, but the New Zealander delivered a standout performance to give the squad food for thought. Nico Hulkenberg also shone in sixth for Audi , followed by Red Bull's Isack Hadjar and Haas driver Oliver Bearman . Fernando Alonso and Alex Albon completed the top 10 on Saturday. George Russell, Mercedes George Russell, Mercedes In Q2 Alonso was the first driver to switch to intermediates as he aimed to lift his Aston Martin out of the belly of the pack. Other soon followed suit, and Russell secured P1 with a 1m26.745s lap on the green-walled compound, ahead of an impressive looking Lawson and Hadjar. Newly-minted world champion Antonelli only just managed to advance in 10th, knocking out Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton , who is already due to start at the rear anyway with a power unit penalty. Oscar Piastri also failed to advance, the McLaren driver a disappointing 12th. Haas rookie Rafael Camara had done well to progress to Q2 despite going off, but he then crashed at the end of the session by going straight into the wall at turn 12, bringing out a late red flag. In the second Racing Bulls car, Arvid Lindblad was dumped out in 14th due to a power unit issue, followed by Carlos Sainz in the Williams . Red Bull's Max Verstappen , who joins Hamilton at the back of the grid with an engine penalty of his own, did not go out in Q2 and was classified 16th. Following an earlier downpour and more rain on the horizon, Q1 started on time but with conditions worsening right before the session went green. Several drivers immediately parked their cars to be pushed back and exchange their intermediates for full wet tyres. Those who did go out confirmed that was a good idea, with cars heading straight back in after reporting aquaplaning as race control red-flagged the session. item.title: Toto Wolff explains the emotional Mercedes factory email leaked online
item.description: Motorsport photo Securing a Formula 1 world championship triggers a lot of emotions, and, usually, a lot of champagne. But for Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff, Kimi Antonelli's historic title win in Mexico City triggered a sudden urge to write an incredibly long essay to his staff. During the Free Practice 3 broadcast at the Brazilian Grand Prix, Sky Sports F1 presenter Simon Lazenby brought up a rather inspiring internal Mercedes email that recently made its way onto the internet. Wolff, in classic deadpan fashion, immediately roasted the broadcaster for actually taking the time to read the whole thing. "Did you read such a long email? It was quite long," Wolff joked. When Lazenby confirmed he read it all the way through, Wolff fired back, "I was surprised the last time I wrote it [something that long] was under severe pressure in school." Deflecting the spotlight Jokes aside, Wolff explained the emotional catalyst behind the massive message. As the guy who officially signed off on putting a teenager into Lewis Hamilton's legendary seat, Wolff was getting flooded with congratulatory messages from the media and the paddock. He didn't want it. "So why was it spontaneous? Because I got so much praise on that Sunday night about giving him the opportunity and in Italy," Wolff explained to the Sky Sports crew. "And it's something that makes you very proud. But I felt I needed to give credit to all the people that maybe weren't so much in the spotlight." Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Formula 1 is the ultimate team sport, and pushing a rookie through a brutal 2025 slump to a 2026 World Championship took an entire village of engineers, strategists, and mentors. Wolff wanted to make sure the men and women turning the wrenches and crunching the data knew this was their trophy, too. "This email, he didn't even give it justice because there is many more that were part of the decision-making process and getting him to where he was," the Mercedes boss continued. "And that's why I felt like I need to at least express my gratitude to the big team." The LinkedIn leak So how did a private, internal factory memo end up public? You can thank Mercedes communications boss and senior leadership figure Bradley Lord for that. When Wolff hit send on his emotional late-night draft, Lord apparently decided the message was far too good to keep locked inside the company inbox. Bradley Lord, Mercedes Deputy Team Principal Bradley Lord, Mercedes Deputy Team Principal "And then Bradley felt that was a more clever email than normally," Wolff laughed. "So he put it on LinkedIn, and that it was when it was spread." It might have been an accidental public relations masterclass, but it offered fans a rare, unscripted look at the nurturing culture Wolff has built inside the Mercedes garage. item.title: Five Things Learned: Nottingham Forest 3-1 Manchester City (Premier League)
item.description: Five Things Learned: Nottingham Forest 3-1 Manchester City (Premier League) City slumped to a third straight Premier League loss with defeat away at Nottingham Forest to fall six points behind reigning champions and leaders Arsenal . Enzo Maresca's side headed into Saturday evening's game at the City Ground on a losing streak, having been defeated by both Aston Villa and Brighton and Hove Albion in recent weeks. Forest, who hadn't scored at home all season, took the lead early on through Jair Cunha, who effortlessly slotted past the out-of-form Gianluigi Donnarumma. After a tepid first-half, the visitors' attack sprang into life as Rayan Cherki smashed in Jeremy Doku's deflected cross to restore hope among the travelling fans. City failed to capitalise on this for the ten minutes following, and Delap instead notched a superb second, finishing off a deadly counter-attack for Forest. Here are five things we learned from Manchester City 's dismal display against Nottingham Forest : 1. Another early goal conceded For a third Premier League game in a row, City conceded from an early goal, putting them behind after just six minutes this time out. There are plenty of issues to highlight from the Nottingham Forest game as well as the past defeats, but the importance of conceding early itself cannot be understated. After taking the lead, the teams work harder and are far harder to break down, whilst the Blues themselves appear to be dejected each time a goal goes in. For previous sides, it would set the hackles up and Manchester City would hit back twice as hard, but this current group seem to struggle to rally back in times of adversity. This is all the more puzzling when you factor in the scenarios the team has already overcome this season, like being a man down at United or conceding three to Sunderland . I think we have all said it multiple times already this campaign, especially in recent weeks, but why on earth, and the wider solar system, is Ayyoub Bouaddi not playing? The Moroccan has looked excellent since joining in the summer, demonstrating the talent to dictate a midfield even at the young age of 19. Despite this, Enzo Maresca continues to select the trio of Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Rayan Cherki for the majority of games. Now there's no doubting the England international has been one of City's best players this season but he is far too exposed in that line-up without the likes of Bouaddi to help cover. This was predictably once again the case versus Nottingham Forest, who sliced through the midfield far too easily to net their goals. item.title: A Bears win on Sunday could catapult Caleb Williams back into the MVP race
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 2: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears reacts after the game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on November 2, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Before the 2026 season started, Caleb Williams was seen as a dark-horse MVP candidate. He was coming off an exciting first year with Ben Johnson, with a highlight reel a mile long. He was the Madden cover athlete, and as the offseason progressed, the buzz around Caleb and the Chicago Bears kept building. After they dropped a 50-burger in Week 1, the NFL shifted the hype train into high gear, and the Bears were the lead story on every NFL show. But then Week 2 and Brian Flores’ Minnesota Vikings defense came to town, and coupled with a steady downpour, Chicago’s offense never got on track. Then a fourth-quarter hamstring injury as the Bears were driving inside the Minnesota 1o yard line would sideline Williams for the next three games, seemingly ending his Most Valuable Player chances. The Bears went 2-1 in his absence, but since his return, Williams and the Bears haven’t trailed in any of their three games, and he’s completing 73.8% of his passes for 860 yards, 4 touchdowns, no turnovers, and a passer rating of 111.3. The last two weeks, he diced up the defenses of the last two Super Bowl teams, and his MVP odds have shot back up according to our partners at FanDuel Sportsbook . Right now, he’s at +800 to win MVP, trailing only the Buffalo Bills’ Josh Allen (+175), the Cincinnati Bengals’ Joe Burrow (+450), the San Fransocso 49ers’ Brock Purdy (+550 ), and the Jacksonville Jaguars’ Trevor Lawrence (+600). Earlier this week, we outlined how difficult it has been historically for a player to win the Most Valuable Player award after missing time during the season, but there is a precedent for him to do it, and another big game on Sunday Night Football could get him back in the conversation.

item.description: Orsolini praise for Bologna coach Palladino is damning for Tedesco Bologna won their fourth game in a row under new coach Raffaele Palladino, as Riccardo Orsolini pins the blame on sacked Domenico Tedesco. ‘We’re enjoying ourselves again.’ The Rossoblu had got off to a truly disastrous start under former Belgium international coach Tedesco, scraping one point from the opening four Serie A matches. We do not have further information at this time.” Ham was transported to the University of Washington’s Medical Center and is currently being treated. No other information is public at this time. Ham, a PA guy who played high school football at Bishop McCourt in Johnstown, has been Penn State ’s radio color commentator since 2000, and has worked with PSU play-by-play man Steve Jones for all of that time. Ham’s best known for what he did on the field, first as an All-American linebacker at Penn State, then one of the greatest NFL linebackers of all time with the Pittsburgh Steelers . In 12 pro seasons, Ham made eight All-Pro teams, earning first team honors every year from 1974-1979. He made it to the second team in 1973 in 1980, so Ham was among the best linebackers in the game for almost a decade straight, helping the Steelers win four Super Bowls and become one of the greatest dynasties in the history of North American sports. Ham was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1988. When people think about Penn State as “Linebacker University,” Ham is one of the first players who made that happen, paving the way for great LBs in the future such as Greg Buttle, Shane Conlan, LaVar Arrington, Paul Posluszny, Dan Connor, NaVorro Bowmam, Tony Rojas and many others. item.title: Titans take clear stance on RB Tony Pollard trade deadline rumors
item.description: Titans take clear stance on RB Tony Pollard trade deadline rumors originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Tennessee Titans are a team to monitor at the 2026 NFL trade deadline, especially following their dealing of Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears . While players like Cam Ward, Wan'Dale Robinson, Carnell Tate, and a few others are clearly untouchable, others like Alontae Taylor and Calvin Ridley are seemingly readily available. But what about someone like Tony Pollard? Conventional wisdom would suggest he's a trade candidate this season, but where do the Titans fall? According to ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport , the Titans have no interest in trading Pollard this season. Titans take clear stand on Tony Pollard trade rumors "The Tennessee Titans are not interested in trading running back Tony Pollard, but they are listening on veteran wide receiver Calvin Ridley, who could be had for a late-round pick," Schefter and Rapoport report. This is a very noteworthy update for the Titans' trade deadline plans. Despite trading Simmons, maybe their best player, they have no plans to trade Pollard as of now. What makes this so interesting is that Pollard is maybe the most obvious trade candidate on their roster. He is a veteran running back who is playing great, is in the final year of his contract, and likely has plenty of suitors. As the Jonathan Taylor sweepstakes unfold, one of the teams that miss out on getting him from the Indianapolis Colts could come to the Titans and offer a strong package to get the second-best running back available for trade. MORE : Joe Burrow joins rare NFL history with six touchdowns despite three interceptions At least, in normal circumstances, that would be the case. Instead, teams like the Denver Broncos , New York Giants , Green Bay Packers , Seattle Seahawks , Minnesota Vikings , and Cincinnati Bengals might have to look elsewhere for RB help. The Titans want to have a good supporting cast for Ward, which is a good idea to get a glimpse of him to better determine if he can be their franchise quarterback. Trading Pollard would hurt the offense in a big way and wouldn't help Ward develop. It makes sense why the Titans might keep Pollard, but for other teams in need of RB help, this stance is some tough news. Fans of the Titans, and any team in need of RB help, shouldn't rule out a trade, just in case a desperate team offers a premium pick for Pollard. But based on this report, it seems unlikely Pollard leaves the Titans this season.
